brief: Three concurrent market risks are building, with the piece noting a fourth would complete a full 'four horsemen' scenario. First, oil: Brent has risen roughly $10 in a month on Middle East tensions, specifically rumored US/Israeli strikes on Iran and reports of ships damaged in the Strait of Hormuz, putting a geopolitical risk premium into crude; European natural gas and electricity prices are climbing too, so the premium risks becoming an inflation problem. Second, France: French 10-year spreads over Germany widened about 50bp in a month, approaching levels last tied to major European financial-stress episodes, with periphery spreads also widening (raising contagion questions) and French equities posting their worst relative performance versus Europe in three decades. Third, AI credit: Nvidia's five-year CDS widened roughly 35bp in a month and hyperscaler CDS is widening broadly, which the note links to circular financing (suppliers, hyperscalers and AI labs funding each other, AI revenue still reliant on recycled capex) even as hyperscaler earnings estimates have stalled since July, semis weaken, and AI-stock concentration nears historical bubble-peak levels, with the SOX's pattern compared to the dot-com bubble.
